Investigation changed the fix

The earlier implementation put a third skeleton diagnostic into a separate display window. Its selector and 144-source checks never exercised a game engine, target, hit or score. The user clarified that both camera views belong with the operator, while one selected camera is for rendering gameplay. Earlier ratings applied to the narrower diagram-selection scope and do not establish acceptance of this correction.

The existing games score in normalized 2D image space. Camera identity and geometry also participate in their body-input/session revisions. The rig fixture contains no complete model for projecting game objects between camera views, and its 2.2 seconds of recorded poses cannot supply fresh input through a three-second start countdown. Reusing one camera's body input beneath another camera's image, or looping old poses as fresh input, would give misleading alignment and ownership.

The correction therefore reuses the existing Slap a Mole engine in explicit Practice/Touch pointer rehearsal. Recorded source observations supply a selected synthetic scene; the pointer controller supplies fresh game input. Both camera diagnostics and reconstructed XYZ stay independent.

Three explicit responsibilities

Operator diagnostics

Both source views appear first, followed by the rig map and XYZ. Samples, rejection reasons and physical planning stay here. A gameplay camera selection cannot replace these views or swap their reconstruction roles.

Authoritative game input

One current-time synthetic pointer/keyboard controller drives the existing game engine. Its player slot, epoch and normalized space are independent of camera-local tracks and recorded rig identity. Recorded bodies and XYZ never award hits.

Player presentation

One selected recorded camera supplies the synthetic background and image geometry. Real mole targets, contact cursor, countdown and score share that geometry. The same stage/HUD moves between an optional inline preview and the player window.

This is genuine game software rehearsal with explicit synthetic controls. It contains no live camera footage or body-driven XYZ gameplay. Displaying the same normalized target under both backgrounds does not establish a shared physical-world target location.

Healthy display switches only update presentation. They retain the current score, target, phase and pointer owner. Missing, stale or uncertain selected presentation pauses affected play and clears the scene; recovery retains the round and uses explicit Resume/countdown. No camera is silently substituted.

Targets, contact cursor and background share one mirrored contain-fit transform. Inverse pointer mapping uses the actual content rectangle and rejects letterboxing. Window moves retain one runtime, one ticker and the operator's monotonic clock. A visible player window can continue when the operator is hidden; physical planning pauses the game and closes its window. The inline preview is collapsed initially to keep two-camera diagnostics prominent.

Before and after, served locally

Before captures use the rig entry, stylesheet and renderer from PR #41's prior commit cc8b13c99fb2af67a4cb7b6ed96c241958ac7b38, with current compatible shared imports and the same recorded solver fixture. They show the earlier third skeleton output. After captures use the corrected real Vite-served application: two primary operator diagnostics and a separate genuine game stage. All source scenes and controls are synthetic.

English desktop, mobile and narrow captures come from a real local Vite server. Synthetic gameplay and diagnostics are labelled; no private participant footage or physical device identities are included.

What remains separate

The current vision service owns one live source. This correction starts no acquisition and adds no simultaneous live camera transport. The selected source is a synthetic scene drawn from recorded 2D observations, rather than RGB footage. Pointer/keyboard inputs provide current game frames; the recorded poses are never looped or retimestamped into fresh body input.

Body-driven multi-view gameplay needs calibrated rig inputs, stable cross-view/session identity and an explicit game-coordinate policy. Image-space targets are not calibrated world-space targets. Physical scale, coverage, exposure synchronization, identity recovery and external motion-to-visible latency still require independent evidence before XYZ can control a maze or depth interactions.

The integration proves one existing Practice/Touch game. Standalone game camera acquisition and other game modes retain their own contracts. Popup creation follows browser policy; blocked popups expose the inline preview, and closing a window restores the same stage. Preference persistence depends on local browser storage. Source-time availability refers to recorded evaluation time, not current exposure or camera performance.

Self-contained static HTML generated by scripts/displayed-camera-report.mjs. Styles and PNG evidence are embedded; optional source/PR links require Internet access. Synthetic examples only. Date uses Asia/Shanghai.
